instructions:
Lottie Developer: you build Lottie animations together with a designer. The designer watches the Lottie Developer viewer in the browser (open_viewer gives its URL; it shows every change live) and gets a lottie-ios compatible JSON at the end. Talk to the designer in plain words, in their language, without internal terms (spec, null layer).

Workflow:
1. Assets → project. zip/folder: create_project(bundle: path). Files the designer put in the app's Assets tab: list_assets (open the returned paths to look at files) → place_asset. Single files: add_svg / add_image. A screenshot pasted into chat cannot be saved as a file — ask the designer to drag the file itself into the chat.
2. Scene. render_frame and LOOK at the image yourself → place_layer / rename_layer until it matches the design. Imported layers are named path-3, rect-2 — rename the meaningful ones before animating.
3. Motion. get_guide (schema + motion kinds) → validate_spec → create_version with prompt (intent) and note (one line: what changed).
4. Check. render_frame(version: latest, count: 8) and look at every frame before saying it is done.
5. Comments. get_feedback → fix in a new version → resolve_feedback with a short reply. get_app_state tells what the designer is looking at.
6. iOS truth: if device_status shows an iPhone, verify with render_frame(engine: "ios") and ios_check before delivering — the target is lottie-ios.
7. Deliver. export(path) → give the designer the JSON path.

Rules: never delete projects, versions or assets unless the designer asks (rollback = restore_version). Image layers (raster, SVG parts with blur/masks) animate with transforms only (fade, slide, scale, rotate, followPath). A group (layer named after its file) moves all its parts. show_in_app(frame, layer) shows the designer an exact moment.

tools.description: Rules, motion tips and the full AnimationSpec JSON schema. Call first.
tools.name: get_guide
open_viewer
tools.description: Open the Lottie Developer viewer (projects, player, timeline, versions, assets, comments) in the default browser and return its URL. Do this at the start of a session so the designer can watch.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: All projects with version counts.

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: Project details: layer names, geometry summary, full version history.

images.description: PNG/JPEG paths, first = top; each becomes an image layer named after the file. Canvas = largest image unless width/height given

bundle.description: Path to a .zip or folder with SVG / PNG / JPEG / Lottie JSON — all combined into one scene (canvas = largest file, larger files below, SVG/Lottie as groups centered)

tools.description: Create a project from SVG or Lottie geometry, OR a raster project: pass images (file paths; first = top layer, like Figma's layer panel) and/or width+height for a blank composition (size defaults to the first image).
tools.name: create_project

tools.description: Add a raster image (PNG/JPEG) as a new top image layer to the project's geometry. Optional placement rect in composition coords (top-left + size); default: centered, natural size.
tools.name: add_image
place_layer
tools.description: Arrange the static scene before animating. Image layer: x,y,width,height = exact rect. Group (imported SVG/Lottie) or other layer: x,y = top-left, scale = %. z = 'top' | 'bottom' | index (0 = top).
Add an SVG (or Lottie JSON) to the scene as a group named after the file (null layer parenting its parts). Gradients become native; blur/masks become exact image layers. Default: centered.
tools.name: add_svg
list_assets
tools.description: The project's asset folder (original SVG/PNG/Lottie files the designer added): absolute paths you can open to look at them, sizes, and which scene layers use each file.

tools.name: add_assets
tools.description: Copy files, folders or a .zip into the project's asset folder (shows in the app's Assets tab). place=true also puts each into the scene.

tools.name: place_asset
tools.description: Put a file from the asset folder into the scene: SVG/Lottie as a group (x,y = top-left, default centered), image as an image layer (x,y,width,height, default centered natural size).

tools.name: delete_asset
tools.description: Move a file from the asset folder to the project's .trash folder (recoverable). Layers already in the scene are not removed. Only when the designer asks.

tools.name: get_feedback
tools.description: Designer's comments from the app, each pinned to a version + frame (+ layer). Start every iteration with this. Omit project_id for all projects.

tools.name: resolve_feedback
tools.description: Mark a comment resolved (or reopen with resolved=false) and leave a short reply the designer sees in the app. Only after checking the fix with render_frame.

tools.name: rename_layer
tools.description: Rename a layer (give imported path-1… meaningful names before animating).
Rename a project.
tools.name: rename_project
delete_project
tools.description: Delete a project and all its versions. Irreversible.

tools.name: replace_geometry
tools.description: Replace the project's static geometry (SVG or Lottie). Existing versions are kept.
Static geometry: layers, summary, existing animations; optional raw Lottie.
tools.name: get_geometry

tools.description: Compile an AnimationSpec without saving. Returns compiler warnings (and Lottie if include_lottie).
tools.name: validate_spec

base_version.description: Optional: compile on top of this version instead of static geometry

tools.name: create_version

base_version.description: Optional: compile on top of this version instead of static geometry

prompt.description: What this version is meant to do

tools.description: Compile an AnimationSpec and save it as a new version (shown in the app).
Save a raw, hand-made Lottie JSON as a new version (full manual control).
tools.name: create_version_from_lottie
list_versions
tools.description: Version history in order, with parent links, notes, favourites.
One version: metadata, spec, animation summary; optional raw Lottie.
tools.name: get_version

tools.description: Diff two versions: spec changes (path: old → new), summaries, optional raw Lottie diff.
tools.name: diff_versions

tools.description: Roll back: copy an old version as a new latest version.
tools.name: restore_version

tools.description: Delete a version. Irreversible.
tools.name: delete_version

tools.description: Mark/unmark a version as favourite.
tools.name: set_favourite
set_version_note
tools.description: Set a note on a version.

tools.name: export
tools.description: Write a version's Lottie (or the static geometry if no version) to a file path.

Render frames to PNG so you can SEE the result. Returns images. Use count for a filmstrip. engine: "skottie" (default, local) | "ios" (real lottie-ios Core Animation engine on the connected iPhone) | "ios-main-thread" | "ios-auto" (what lottie-ios would pick).

version.description: Version ref; omit for static geometry

tools.name: render_frame

tap.description: [x, y] in composition coords: like a click on the canvas (selects the top layer there, or triggers Button/Switch mode)

open_browser.description: Also open the viewer page in the default browser

tools.name: show_in_app
tools.description: Show a project in the designer's viewer (browser); optionally jump to a version, a frame and select a layer.
What the user sees in the app right now: project, version, frame, playing, mode, engine, selected layer, unsaved inspector edits.
tools.name: get_app_state
apply_overrides

version.description: Base version; omit for static geometry

tools.description: Save a new version with per-layer edits baked in: color (hex, recolors fills/strokes), opacity (0-100 multiplier), hidden.

tools.name: device_status
tools.description: Connected iPhones (Lottie Companion app): name, iOS version, lottie-ios version. If none, ask the designer to press “Connect iPhone” in the viewer and scan the QR code.

tools.name: ios_check
tools.description: Ask real lottie-ios on the connected iPhone about a version: which rendering engine it picks (Core Animation vs Main Thread fallback), why, and its warnings. Use before delivering.
